principles: Fix the check, not the guard that caught it (budget stays)
Canonicalization must mirror the proven self-branch mechanism (git worktree list)
Genuine mismatch detection must survive intact
drivers: DONE-required npm test red from every story worktree
False Relink advice erodes doctor trust
Worktree builds are the documented dev practice (dev-memory 148297b)

options.name: canonicalize-nonself-expected
pros: Root-cause fix mirroring existing self-branch logic
Keeps budget guard and genuine warn
cons: Adds a git invocation per doctor run in non-self contexts

options.name: raise-smoke-budget
cons: Hides the false warn; erodes B-7c05 brief UX guard; warn still misleads operators

options.name: relink-global-per-worktree
cons: Contradicts documented practice; breaks other worktrees and main; manual toil per story

rationale: Only the first option removes the structurally guaranteed false warn while preserving both the brief byte budget and genuine mismatch detection, and it reuses the exact canonicalization pattern already proven in the self-project branch.

preMortem.scenario: git worktree list fails in non-git or bare contexts and the new path crashes doctor
preMortem.trigger: doctor run in a directory without git or with a bare repo
preMortem.mitigation: Fall back to the current un-canonicalized corePackageRoot on any git failure (behavior identical to today); edge intent covers non-git fallback

preMortem.scenario: Canonicalization masks a genuine mismatch (global pointing at a different clone of the same project)
preMortem.trigger: Two separate clones; global linked to clone A, running clone B worktree build
preMortem.mitigation: Canonicalize via the repository CONTAINING corePackageRoot only — a different clone has a different repo root, so its canonical path differs and the warn still fires; adversarial test pins this

preMortem.scenario: Extra git invocation slows doctor in brief paths
preMortem.trigger: doctor called in tight loops or CI
preMortem.mitigation: Single additional git worktree list only on the non-self branch, mirroring the cost already accepted on the self branch; no loop

preMortem.scenario: Self-branch behavior accidentally altered while refactoring shared helper
preMortem.trigger: Extracting a common canonicalizer changes expectedSelfCoreRoot semantics
preMortem.consequence: Regressions in the previously working self-project doctor
preMortem.mitigation: Edge intent asserts self-context output unchanged; keep expectedSelfCoreRoot call sites untouched or covered by tests
